questions.q: Who created Bahadur, the home-grown hero of an Indian comics line?
questions.why: Aabid Surti dreamed up Bahadur and pitched him to the publisher while freelancing for Bennett, Coleman & Co.

questions.q: Which publisher's imprint carried Bahadur's adventures until it stopped publishing in 1990?
questions.why: Bahadur ran in Indrajal Comics, the Bennett, Coleman & Co. line, and ended when that line was discontinued in 1990.

questions.q: In which year did Bahadur first appear in print?
questions.why: Bahadur debuted in December 1976, created to give Indian readers a local hero beside imported ones like the Phantom.

questions.q: Bahadur's father was a dacoit killed in a clash with police. What was his name?
questions.why: Bhairav Singh died fighting the police, which set the teenage Bahadur on his first path of revenge.

questions.q: Which police officer, who had shot Bahadur's father, adopted the teenage Bahadur?
questions.why: Officer Vishal took in the boy after the shootout, and Bahadur eventually sided with the law.

questions.q: What is the name of the civilian outfit Bahadur founded to help police fight bandits?
questions.why: Bahadur created the Citizen's Security Force, called Naagrik Suraksha Dal in Hindi, which assists police against dacoits.

questions.q: Who is Bahadur's helper, a reformed dacoit who surrendered to the police?
questions.why: Lakhan gave up banditry, surrendered, and became Bahadur's trusted assistant.

questions.q: Which martial artist is Bahadur's love interest who fights alongside him?
questions.why: Bela is the martial-arts expert who stands with Bahadur in the Indrajal Comics stories.

questions.q: Which outfit did the series' author give Bahadur to blend Indianness and Western-style progress?
questions.why: Surti explained that the saffron kurta stands for Indianness, while the jeans, a Western import, signal progress.

questions.q: Early Bahadur stories were inspired by the dacoits of which notorious region?
questions.why: The ravines of the Chambal Valley, famed for bandits, shaped the early adventures set around the small town of Jaigarh.
